item.title: River Kayaking & Canoeing in Miyazaki — Guide
item.description: Miyazaki’s mountainous interior is laced with beautiful, clear rivers that make superb settings for kayaking and canoeing. On the scenic Gokase River near Takachiho and other inland waterways, guided tours let paddlers glide across calm, emerald-green stretches of water framed by forested gorges, cliffs and greenery, taking in the pristine scenery from the water at a gentle pace. Suitable for beginners, families and experienced paddlers alike, the tours typically provide all equipment and a guide, and range from relaxing flat-water paddles on rivers and reservoirs to more adventurous stretches.

item.title: River Kayaking and Canyoning in Saga — Guide
item.description: For an active, adventurous side of Saga, the rivers and gorges of the mountainous south offer kayaking and canyoning. Guided kayak tours let you paddle across calm rivers and reservoirs among forested hills, gliding on clear water and taking in the peaceful scenery at your own pace — suitable for beginners with a guide. For more of a thrill, canyoning (or ‘shower climbing’) tours take you into the mountain gorges to scramble, wade, slide down natural rock chutes and jump into clear pools beneath waterfalls, wearing a wetsuit and helmet — a wet, exhilarating way to experience the wild river landscape.

item.title: Sea Kayaking Around Naruto — Guide
item.description: The coast around Naruto, where the Seto Inland Sea meets the Pacific, offers scenic sea kayaking amid island scenery, quiet coves and views of the great Onaruto Bridge. Guided kayak tours let you paddle the calmer sheltered waters away from the fierce tidal race of the strait itself, gliding along the coastline, exploring inlets and small beaches, and taking in the sea and bridge from water level. Suitable for beginners with a guide, it’s a peaceful yet active way to experience the beautiful Naruto seascape up close, quite different from the roar of the whirlpools nearby.

item.title: Okutama Guide: Tokyo's Wild Mountain Frontier
item.description: Most people are astonished to learn that Tokyo — the word that means glass towers and 37 million people — also contains genuine mountain wilderness. Travel two hours west of Shinjuku and the metropolis gives way entirely to steep forested valleys, crystal-clear rivers, a turquoise reservoir, and limestone caves: this is Okutama, the mountainous far-western edge of Tokyo Prefecture, part of the Chichibu-Tama-Kai National Park. Here you can kayak on a mountain lake, walk through a gorge, descend into a cave, soak in a hot spring, and stand among some of the Kanto region’s finest autumn colour — all without leaving Tokyo.

item.title: Saitama Leisure: Railway Museum, Chichibu Whisky & River Activities
item.description: Saitama sits immediately north of Tokyo, but it rarely appears on the itinerary of visitors who spend their week navigating Shinjuku, Asakusa and Shibuya. That is a significant missed opportunity. Within 30 to 90 minutes of central Tokyo, Saitama offers a railway museum that rivals anything in Europe, one of the world’s most respected whisky distilleries, wild river activities in a dramatic gorge, the quiet contemplative world of Japan’s bonsai capital, and a compact historic town made for slow café-hopping.
